verified_claims: Task: fault detection indicative of geothermal resources, not direct vent/reservoir discovery.
Initial test labels are expert-identified faults absent from the current public USGS database.
Provided numerical feature GeoTIFF is EPSG:32611 at 100 m resolution.
Distance-weighted TP is a maximum of p(x) times a triangular kernel over predictions around each truth pixel; FP uses distance to the truth; FN is truth mass minus weighted TP.
Triangular radius is 300 m; alpha is 0.2 and beta is 0.8.
Submission: single-layer float32 GeoTIFF, confidence values between 0 and 1, same CRS, resolution and bounds. Text says data outside bounds is null or NaN.
limits: Page access does not authenticate the owner-mirrored data bytes.
A local validator cannot prove remote portal acceptance.

sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey, ScienceBase data release
sources.access: ScienceBase summary, release metadata, and attached-file listing read on 2026-10-22; direct binary fetch attempted via fetch_page and returned HTTP 500.
sources.license_as_published: No explicit license statement was found in the page text reviewed; source is a public USGS data-release listing.
verified_claims: The release provides estimated background conductive heat-flow maps made with a weighted 2D LOESS procedure that de-emphasizes measurements judged convectively influenced.
The point coverage includes a well residual measuring departure from estimated background heat flow; the USGS description says residuals may help identify hydrothermal or groundwater influence.
ScienceBase lists a public ZIP of 124.12 MB and publishes its MD5, but neither the ZIP nor its contents were downloaded here.
limits: Residuals are not fault labels and can reflect groundwater circulation, lithology, well quality, and measurement uncertainty.
The maps were intentionally designed to estimate background conductive heat flow, not to map every convective anomaly.
No SHA-256 or grid compatibility is claimed until the binary is fetched and verified.

sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey, ScienceBase data release
sources.access: ScienceBase summary and attached-file listings (chunks 0-1) read on 2026-10-22; no raster binary downloaded.
verified_claims: The release estimates electrical conductance from a 3D inversion of more than 800 publicly available magnetotelluric transfer functions.
Five GeoTIFFs are listed for depth intervals 2–12 km, 12–20 km, 20–50 km, 50–90 km, and 90–200 km; each listing shows a 3.94 MB raster in native CRS EPSG:4269.
The USGS description says these conductance maps are intended to inform subsurface fluids and fluid pathways.
limits: The inverse-model grid resolution and effective spatial support have not been compared with the 100 m competition grid; resampling would not create 100 m information.
Conductive lithology, saline basin fill, and inversion smoothing can mimic or blur fault-related fluid pathways.
No binary download, alignment, or candidate score is claimed.

sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey, ScienceBase data release
sources.access: ScienceBase summary and attached-file listing read on 2026-10-22; no shapefile binary downloaded.
verified_claims: The release reports slip- and dilation-tendency calculations for Quaternary fault segments and includes fault geometry and stress inputs.
USGS says the fault segments came from a publicly available database modified after the USGS Quaternary Fault and Fold Database; the listing offers 34.25 MB and 27.35 MB study-area shapefile ZIPs.
limits: Because the feature geometries are derived from Qfault, rasterizing these tendencies for a hide-and-recover holdout would expose the target catalogue and is not eligible as an independent feature.
Use as literature/context only unless a stress tensor independent of fault geometries can be obtained and separately validated.
